title: Checkout cost versus net cost
hook: A refundable deposit changes checkout cash without changing the modeled net price.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Separate upfront deposits from net cost after a stated full refund.

misconception: Upfront cash paid and net cost after refunds are always the same.
objective: Separate upfront deposits from net cost after a stated full refund.

claims.text: Each item is €2.40 plus a fictional €0.25 deposit, refunded in full on return. Scaled model; fictional deposit; full return assumed.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Containers=4, A=€9.6 and B=€10.6. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",2.4,"x"]; B=["*",2.65,"x"]; x denotes Containers. At x=4, A=9.6, B=10.6. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The checkout includes a deposit for each container. The after-return amount subtracts those same deposits. These are different moments in the arithmetic; the scenario does not describe any region’s actual deposit law.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",2.4,"x"]; B=["*",2.65,"x"]; x denotes Containers. At x=4, A=9.6, B=10.6. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: Each item is €2.40 plus a fictional €0.25 deposit, refunded in full on return. You buy ten and return all ten containers. What are the checkout and after-return amounts? Correct: €26.50 at checkout, €24.00 after return. The checkout includes ten €0.25 deposits; the return takes the same €2.50 back. They are two different moments.
